rules.note: Most clauses place the verb at the end of the sentence (e.g., ama manu paka, sol hulm nasiru).
Simple S‑V‑O clauses without an initial adverbial sometimes have the verb immediately after the subject (e.g., mi gedo vela, nesh mi tolv velen).
The suffix ‑ma marks a locative relationship on nouns (office‑ma, vessa‑ma).
The suffix ‑en appears on verbs to indicate past tense (khanen, tamirensa).
The suffix ‑sa marks future tense on verbs (khanirusa, tamirusa).
The negation particle na follows the verb and precedes the object (mi so na deken, so chenn na loba).
When the honorific second‑person pronoun tavo is used, the verb takes the suffix ‑sa regardless of tense (tavo manu khanirusa, tavo office tamensa).
